---
title: "Underfitting"
description: "A model underfits when it fails to capture patterns needed to perform well even on its training data."
term: "Underfitting"
letter: "U"
category: "Machine Learning"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

Underfitting happens when a model is too limited or too poorly trained to
learn useful patterns. It performs poorly not only on new examples but
often on the training data too.

## Technical explanation

Underfitting is associated with high bias or insufficient optimization,
features, or model capacity relative to the task. Training and validation
errors may both remain high, though reliable diagnosis depends on
appropriate data and metrics.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

An underfit model may be inexpensive and stable but fail to meet task
requirements. Diagnosing it helps teams decide whether to improve features,
increase capacity, train longer, or revise the objective.

## How it works

Compare training and validation performance against a simple baseline and
the target requirement. If both are poor, investigate data quality,
features, optimization, and model capacity before increasing complexity.
Changes should be evaluated on held-out data.

## Practical example

A linear model may be unable to capture a nonlinear relationship in the
data. Adding appropriate nonlinear features or using a more expressive
model can reduce training error, after which validation performance checks
whether generalization also improves.

## Common misconceptions

- Underfitting is not simply “a model with too few parameters”; poor data,
  objectives, optimization, or features can cause it too.
- Increasing model size may reduce training error but does not guarantee
  lower validation error.
